item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Mon Oct 5 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Sparkdate: Tellus AfterDark — Tue Oct 6, 6:30 PM — Tellus360
item.description:
A downtown Lancaster staple with a rooftop that turns any night into something worth dressing up for. Open sky, string lights, and a bar that’s easy to linger at — the kind of place that does half the work of making people comfortable before anyone even says hello. Add real conversations instead of small talk that goes nowhere, and you’ve got a night built for singles who actually want to meet someone, not just match with them.
How the night works:Check in with a host and get a name tag — there’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements:First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play — that’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. Then the structure drops away and it’s open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it’s working. By that point you’ve already met mos

item.title: Redemption Time — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Join us at the Ware Center for a free screening of the film Redemption Time—plus a community discussion panel and a Q&A with the filmmakers. Witness a powerful multimedia performance film featuring poet Jimmy Santiago Baca and jazz violinist Christian Howes, two formerly incarcerated artists who reclaimed their lives through art. Combining spoken word, music, and visual art, Redemption Time invites audiences into a shared space of healing and transformation.
Come early for a pre-show community panel at 6:15 pm, and stay after the film for a post-screening Q&A with Dr. David Gonzalez, director of Redemption Time, and Christian Howes, a formerly incarcerated individual featured in Redemption Time and an award-winning jazz violinist. Admission is free! Tickets are required for entry.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Revolution to Reconstruction with Clint Smith — Wed Oct 7, 5:00 PM — LancasterHistory
item.description:
LancasterHistory will welcome award-winning author Clint Smith to the Ware Center for Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality. Smith, author of How the Word Is Passed and Above Ground, will explore Pennsylvania’s central role in shaping our nation’s evolving ideals of liberty and equality. The event will include a lecture followed by Q&A. Pocket Books will also be on site selling signed copies of How the word is passed. The lecture is FREE, but advance registration is required and space is limited.
